0.0.n: 年 follows a number to indicate a calendar year.

0.1.n: Combined with 月, this number names January.

0.2.n: 月 follows 1 here to name January, rather than a duration of one month.

0.3.n: から marks January as the starting point of the edition’s date range.

0.4.n: Combined with 月, this number names March.

0.5.n: 月 combines with 3 to name March; 版 labels this as the edition covering January through March.

1.0.n: 最新 describes the current affairs questions as up to date.

1.1.n: 時事 comes before 問題 to specify that the questions concern recent events.

1.2.n: 問題 refers to quiz questions here, not difficulties or troubles.

1.3.n: 選 after a number labels a curated selection, without necessarily implying a ranking.

2.0.n: この must come before a noun; here it points to the video being watched.

2.1.n: 動画 is the topic of the sentence, marked by は.

2.2.n: は marks what the sentence is about, rather than who performs the action.

2.4.n: The て-form of 聞き流す connects casual listening with memorizing; here it suggests listening without focused study.

2.5.n: The plain form comes before こと, referring to memorizing the material presented in the video.

2.6.n: こと turns 覚える into an activity that can be discussed as possible.

2.7.n: も presents learning by listening as an additional option.

2.8.n: できます is the polite form of できる; after a verb plus こと, it expresses ability or possibility.

3.0.n: それでは signals a transition from the introduction to the main content.

3.1.n: 参ります is the polite form of humble 参る, meaning go or come; here it formally announces getting started.

0.tip: から marks the start of the range; March is understood as its endpoint even without まで.

1.tip: A number followed by 選 means that many selected items, not necessarily ranked items.

2.lit: As for this video, listening casually and memorizing is also possible.
2.tip: A plain verb plus ことができます means can do; here も replaces が to add also.

3.tip: 参ります makes this transition sound formal and courteous, rather than describing a literal journey.
